html:
Indigenous leader who led the largest rebellion against Spanish rule in the Andes, in 1780 and 1781. Born José Gabriel Condorcanqui, he was a local chief near Cusco and a mule train owner. He took the name of the last Inca ruler, Túpac Amaru, executed by the Spanish in 1572, from whom he claimed descent.

In November 1780 he seized and hanged a hated Spanish official. He demanded an end to forced sales of goods to Indigenous people and to the mita, the forced labour draft for the mines of Potosí. Tens of thousands joined him, and his wife Micaela Bastidas was one of his chief organisers. His army failed to take Cusco.

In 1781 he was betrayed and captured. In Cusco's main square he was made to watch the execution of his wife and son, then was torn by horses and beheaded. The rising went on under Túpac Katari, who besieged La Paz. Spain crushed it with great bloodshed, but it shook Peru and is remembered as a forerunner of independence.
